title: Dustin May agrees to $52 million deal with White Sox as Brewers get raided again

 Gabe Lacques USA TODAY Updated Nov. 17, 2026, 11:45 a.m. ET Hear this story Dustin May didn't quite nail down a playoff rotation spot with the World Series-bound Milwaukee Brewers . But he showed enough in his bounceback year between St. Louis and Milwaukee to earn a significant payday from another team on the rise.
 May and the White Sox are in agreement on a three-year, $52 million deal, bringing the fireballing right-handed pitcher into a Chicago pitching staff that desperately needs more length and shutdown ability.
 A person with direct knowledge of the deal confirmed to USA TODAY Sports that May and the White Sox are in agreement. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the deal, first reported by FanSided, is not yet official.
 May, 29, becomes the second Brewers free agent to defect from the World Series champions, after first baseman Jake Bauers signed a four-year, $58 million deal with the Boston Red Sox .
 May has long featured a fastball that has averaged as much as 98 mph, and he was a valued young member of the Los Angeles Dodgers ' rotation, earning a World Series ring in 2020. But Tommy John surgery and a freak esophygeal injury waylaid his Dodgers career and he posted a 4.96 ERA between Los Angeles and Boston in 2025.

The Cardinals signed him to a one-year, $12 million deal and he pitched well, nearly throwing a perfect game and pumping his trade value sufficiently to garner a trade to the first-place Brewers. He posted a 5.65 ERA in 10 starts and was relegated to the bullpen in the postseason.
 But he came up clutch in October, covering four crucial innings in their NLCS conquest of the Dodgers and aiding their comeback from a four-run deficit in Game 2 of the World Series. He also started Game 4, giving up two runs in three innings.
 With the White Sox, May becomes practically their most accomplished starting pitcher. As the club made a surprise run to the American League Division Series, they deployed almost all bullpen games in the postseason, with nominal ace Sean Burke following an opener. The club recently announced top reliever Grant Taylor would aim to join the rotation in 2027, giving the White Sox an interesting nucleus: May, Burke and Taylor.
 May struck out nearly nine batters per nine innings this past season, perhaps the most attractive asset he brought to the market in an era that highly prioritizes swing-and-miss. The White Sox are betting on his stuff - he averaged nearly 97 mph on a sinker that he throws nearly a quarter of the time - and further progress from the rare under-30 arm that hits the free agent market.
